newsitem.title: FRANCE: French pilot hurt in Italy crash dies of wounds.
newsitem.headline: French pilot hurt in Italy crash dies of wounds.

text.p: A French pilot critically injured when his plane overshot a runway at Florence airport in Italy earlier this week died in hospital in Marseille on Saturday, French radio said.
Jean-Remi Cuculiere of Montpellier-based Air Littoral was flown home on Friday in a coma following Wednesday's accident and the airline had said his condition had worsened.
The pilot, aged 50 and with about 10,000 flying hours experience, suffered from multiple fractures and head injuries, French media said.
He was returned to France with the co-pilot of the ATR-42 turbo prop plane, Alain Blayes, who sustained minor injuries in the crash. Five of the 14 passengers were also hurt.

The flight, arriving from Nice, failed to stop at the end of the runway after landing at Florence's small airport. The plane broke through a perimeter fence and ploughed on towards a motorway, hitting the road's guard rail with its nose.
Italian magistrates have begun an investigation of the accident.
